subject: SIG questionnaire — data handling deep dive and evidence pack
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.co>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up — data handling: prompt logs, retention, training

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the time to work through the SIG — we’re down to a few open questions on data handling for our procurement/security review. Can you confirm the following in writing (we need text we can include in the vendor risk binder and push to legal):

1) Prompt and request-response logs: what exactly is retained by default, where is it stored, and how long is it kept?
2) Are prompt logs, unredacted customer inputs or outputs, ever used to train Redwood models or shared with model training pipelines? If so, under what contractual opt-in?
3) Do you offer configuration to disable prompt logging or immediately purge session content on a per-account basis? If so, please provide the config or API names we can use.
4) Evidence: can you attach a short statement we can add to our SIG answers and any supporting artifacts (SOC 2 link, sample log export headers, encryption/KMS details)?

Appreciate concise, explicit responses — procurement wants a single-paragraph attestation we can attach, plus a technical snippet for eng to implement.

Thanks,
Jordan
Security Engineer, Acme Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.co>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.co, rishi_malhotra@redwood.co
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — data handling: prompt logs, retention, training

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise, attestation-ready answers plus pointers to attached artifacts. I’ve also attached a small config snippet you can hand to engineering. Let me know if you want this language embedded verbatim into the SIG spreadsheet.

Attestation (single paragraph) — you can copy/paste this into your binder: 
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided prompts, inputs, or outputs for model training unless the customer has explicitly opted in via a documented contractual agreement (e.g., Data Processing Addendum or training opt-in addendum). By default, request/response logs are ephemeral: metadata and telemetry required for routing are retained for 30 days, while full request/response content is retained for operational debugging for up to 7 days unless the customer configures a shorter window or enables immediate purge. All logs are encrypted in transit and at rest, stored in the customer’s region when Private/VPC options are used, and access is role-restricted to authorized operations staff. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited; supporting artifacts are provided."

Clarifications / tech specifics: 
- Default retention windows:
  • Full request/response payloads (unredacted): 7 days default (configurable to 0–90 days per-account)
  • Operational telemetry / routing metadata: 30 days default
- Storage & encryption:
  • Stored in encrypted object stores with AES-256 at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit.
  • Customer-managed KMS available for Dedicated/Private.
- Training & model updates:
  • No training on customer data by default. Customer must opt in via an explicit contractual flag.
  • Any opt-in for training is auditable and subject to scope limits; we provide an export of artifacts used for model improvement.
- Configuration / API: sample attached (sample_no_training_config.yaml). Key flags: no_training: true; log_retention_days: 0; prompt_redaction: strict.

Attachments included: redwood_SIG_answers_20260830.pdf (attestation + filled SIG spreadsheet), sample_no_training_config.yaml, redwood_evidence_pack_links.txt (SOC2 link, doorstop architecture diagram, sample log export headers).

If you want, I can also provide a short one-sentence contract clause our legal team recommends for the DPA to be explicit. Otherwise, I’ll coordinate with Rishi (cc’d) if you need a signed attestation on company letterhead.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.co
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.co>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — data handling: prompt logs, retention, training

Thanks Soojin — that language is exactly what procurement/legal wanted. A couple quick follow-ups:

- Can we get a signed attestation on company letterhead saying Redwood will not use Acme Health data for training without written opt-in? We’d like that for our legal file.
- Engineer asked for the exact API key/endpoint names for the no_training mode so they can tie it to our provisioning scripts. The sample YAML helps, but they want REST call names if they’re different.

If possible, we’d like the letter and a one-line clause we can paste into our DPA.

Jordan

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.co>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.co, marissa_cole@redwood.co
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — data handling: prompt logs, retention, training

Jordan —

We can do both.

1) Signed attestation: attaching redwood_SIG_answers_20260830.pdf which includes the same attestation text on Redwood letterhead with signature from our Head of Security. If you need a countersigned DPA, Rishi is looped in to expedite.

2) Engineering names / API details: for immediate configuration your engineering team can call the Control Plane API (examples below). The sample YAML maps to the same fields.

  • PATCH /v1/accounts/{account_id}/settings
    payload: { "no_training": true, "log_retention_days": 0, "prompt_redaction": "strict" }

  • POST /v1/accounts/{account_id}/actions/purge-session
    payload: { "session_id": "<session-id>", "immediate": true }

  • Role-based access: only org-admin + security-role can change these flags; we can provide an IAM binding example.

3) One-line DPA clause you can paste: 
"Vendor does not use Customer-provided prompts, inputs, or outputs for model training or improvement absent explicit, documented, and auditable written consent from Customer."

Rishi / Marissa — please confirm we’re OK to send the signed PDF to Acme and to provide the API IAM example. If you prefer, I can redact internal contact details before sending.

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
